tasks.short: Write procedures, explain them in toolbox meetings, collect attendance, inspect sites and record findings.

steps.what: Supervisor writes operating procedures and work standards for safe working
Supervisor explains procedures to crews in toolbox meetings
Crew members sign toolbox attendance on their phones in the field app
Supervisor collects attendance signatures: on paper today; after the change checks the phone sign-in list against who attended and chases missing signatures
Supervisor inspects work sites to enforce safe working and performance standards
Supervisor writes inspection findings: on a paper form today, on a checklist with photos in the field app after the change

tasks.design: Crews sign toolbox attendance on their phones in the field app ({OPS_SYSTEM}), and the supervisor checks the sign-in list. Inspections are recorded on a checklist with photos in the same app, which takes as long as the paper form. Writing procedures, explaining them and inspecting stay with the supervisor; findings are about work and safety, not used to rate individuals.
tasks.previous_blocker: Attendance and inspections were on paper forms.
tasks.enabler_now: Field apps offer inspection checklists with photos and digital sign-in.
tasks.still_hard: Safe working depends on habits, not records.
tasks.human_edge: Stopping a worker who is about to cut a branch above their head.

reach.learn: Whether digital records make audits faster.

evidence.claim: The FacilityApps quality control app offers predefined inspection forms, photos as evidence and reports for clients.
Inspection results tied to named workers can check performance, so the works council must consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from writing procedures to recorded inspections; incident investigation is outside.
Input contract: work risks from the firm's risk assessment; checklists set by the supervisor; fallback is paper.

Writing, explaining, inspecting and writing findings keep their full time; findings are the supervisor's own first record. s3 keeps 20 for checking the sign-in list and chasing missing signatures. Crews' sign-in is shown as s3a.
research_questions: Are safety records complete at audits?

incremental.description: Supervisor updates the app checklists when procedures change.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many crew members forget to sign on the phone, so the supervisor still collects about half on paper and s3 keeps 60 (3.1); high: crews sign in the app (6.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: List due jobs, check crew and equipment availability, check the weather, build the week schedule, publish it to crews and reschedule after rain or breakdowns.

steps.what: Supervisor lists jobs due this week from contracts and requests: in a spreadsheet today; after the change enters client requests and reads the due list the system builds
Supervisor checks crew and equipment availability: by phone today; after the change reads leave and machine bookings in the system and phones only about late changes
Supervisor checks weather conditions and decides which work can go ahead
Supervisor schedules work for crews on the planning board
Supervisor checks the final week schedule before pushing: each crew's jobs, sites, machines and days
Supervisor publishes the schedule: phones crews and posts the plan in the group chat today; pushes it once to crew phones after the change
Supervisor reschedules after rain or breakdowns

tasks.design: The planning system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) lists due jobs from contract frequencies and client requests, shows crew leave and machine bookings, and flags jobs the forecast rules out (no spraying in wind, no mowing in heavy rain). Fixed rules propose a week schedule by skills, equipment and travel distance, never by individual speed or behaviour; the supervisor adjusts it, and only then is it pushed to crew phones. Rescheduling after rain or breakdowns stays with the supervisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Due work, availability and weather were pieced together in spreadsheets and calls.
tasks.enabler_now: Planning tools hold contract frequencies, availability and rules, and push schedules to phones.
tasks.still_hard: Dutch weather changes plans daily; the supervisor still juggles.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which client will accept a delay and which will not.
tasks.altitude: The supervisor adjusts a proposed schedule instead of building it.

reach.learn: Whether phone schedules cut morning calls.

evidence.claim: FacilityApps schedules per site and employee with working-time and cao checks.
An AI system that allocates tasks on behaviour or personal traits is high-risk; rule-based scheduling on skills and distance is not.
A roster scheme sets working times and needs works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from due jobs to the changed schedule; client invoicing is outside.
Input contract: contract frequencies from client contracts; leave from the HR system; machine bookings by the workshop; fallback is the spreadsheet.

Rescheduling and the check before pushing keep their full time. s1 keeps 10 for entering client requests and reading the due list; s2 keeps 10 for calls about late changes; s3 keeps 50 because the forecast flags replace looking up the weather per job while deciding stays; s4 keeps 50 because the proposal fills crews and routes and the supervisor adjusts it; s5 keeps 10 for the release.

incremental.description: Supervisor keeps job types and weather rules current.

approvals.approved_version: The week schedule with each crew's jobs, sites, machines and days exactly as checked by the supervisor in s5c, pushed once to crew phones in the planning system; any change needs a new check before it is pushed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: leave and machine bookings are often not in the system and the proposal needs heavy rework, so s1 and s2 keep 40 and s4 keeps 70 (40.1); high: the system holds current data and the proposal needs only adjustments (54.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Brief crews, visit sites to direct work, answer crew questions, deal with clients on site and note the day's work.

steps.what: Supervisor briefs crews at the start of the day
Supervisor directs activities of workers pruning trees and shrubs and cultivating lawns on site
Supervisor answers crew questions about the job by phone
Supervisor deals with clients on site
Supervisor writes daily job notes: on paper today, in the field app with photos after the change

tasks.design: Each job in the field app ({OPS_SYSTEM}) carries the planting plan, client wishes and earlier notes, so crews find answers there and call less. The supervisor writes job notes with photos in the app instead of on paper, which takes as long. Briefing, directing and talking with clients stay in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Job details lived in the supervisor's head and on paper notes.
tasks.enabler_now: Field apps hold job details, plans and photos per site.
tasks.still_hard: Many questions are judgement calls only the supervisor can make.
tasks.human_edge: Showing a new worker how far to cut back a shrub.

reach.learn: Whether job details in the app cut calls.

evidence.claim: FacilityApps offers digital work orders per site.

assumptions: Boundary: from the briefing to job notes; invoicing is outside.
Input contract: planting plans and client wishes from the contract; fallback is paper notes.

Briefing, directing, client talks and writing job notes keep their full time; job notes are the supervisor's own first record. s3 keeps 70 because crews find the planting plan and client wishes in the app and call less.

incremental.description: Supervisor keeps job details current in the app.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: job details in the app are often incomplete, so crews keep calling and s3 keeps 85 (1.2); high: crews find most answers in the app (3.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Demonstrate techniques, watch and correct practice, record who is trained on which machine and prepare instruction sheets.

steps.what: Supervisor trains workers in pruning trees, caring for turf and using equipment by demonstration
Supervisor watches workers practise and corrects them
Supervisor keeps a list of who is trained on which machine: on paper today; after the change records each training in the learning system, which works out refresher dates
Supervisor writes instruction sheets for machines

tasks.design: Training per machine and technique is recorded in the learning system ({LMS}) instead of on paper, which shows who may use which machine and when refreshers are due. Makers' manuals are linked per machine in the field app, so instruction sheets only add the firm's own points. Demonstrating and correcting stay in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Training was tracked on a paper list and instruction sheets written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning systems record training per machine with refresher dates.
tasks.still_hard: Skill shows in the work, not in the record.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a worker holds the chainsaw too close to the body.

reach.learn: Whether training records prevent untrained use.

evidence.claim: Learning systems record training per machine with refresher dates.
Employers must instruct workers on the safe use of equipment.

assumptions: Boundary: from training need to records and instruction sheets; certified courses are outside.
Input contract: makers' manuals from the equipment suppliers; machine list from the workshop; fallback is paper.

Demonstrating and correcting keep their full time. s3 keeps 70 because recording each training stays and only rewriting the list and working out refresher dates drop. s4 keeps 70 because makers' content is linked and the supervisor writes only the firm's own points.
Records are about skills, not used to rate workers.
unknowns: Machines that need a training record.

incremental.description: Supervisor links the maker's manual when a new machine arrives.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: refreshers are rare and many machines lack a usable manual, so s3 keeps 90 and s4 keeps 85 (3.0); high: refreshers are tracked and manuals are linked (7.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The groundskeeping supervisor keeps directing, teaching and safety; spreadsheet schedules, calls and paper records shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A supervisor who spends mornings on site instead of on the phone.

job.title: First-Line Supervisors of Landscaping, Lawn Service, and Groundskeeping Workers
